[1/2] Make layout_hash fingerprint every seeded prop (merchants, traps, sconces, rooms, biome) and add unit tests; [2/2] add a harness selftest that reads a Scroll of Inferno on a visible enemy and asserts damage, consumption and a turn advance (closes reforge run-3 findings)

impact_assessment.why: The last reforge review left two open findings: layout_hash claims to fingerprint everything the seeded generator decides but omits merchants, traps and sconces, and the shipped Scroll of Inferno branch has no browser test, so deleting it would pass the suite
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent can trust layout_hash to detect any seeded layout change, and the scroll branch is proven through the shipped engine instead of only by reading the source
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the harness state gains traps, sconces and rooms; layout_hash values change once; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: read-only harness, no game save change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Unit tests mutate each seeded prop and require a different hash; the scroll check drives the real engine in headless Edge and asserts damage, item consumption and turn advance; full unit, harness and inspector gates

[1/3] Re-plan: expose a validated public use_item action; [2/3] dispatch it to the shipped useInventoryItem with an out-of-range error; [3/3] move the Scroll of Inferno selftest onto the public action, document the index contract and run the gates

impact_assessment.why: The new scroll check calls useInventoryItem directly, so an agent driving the documented play command still cannot use a potion, scroll or piece of gear; the public harness has no action for the branch it now proves
impact_assessment.benefits: Agents can equip loot, drink potions and read scrolls through the same validated JSON action path as movement and abilities; the scroll proof exercises that path instead of an internal call
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the action catalog gains use_item with a zero-based index; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the action reads the existing inventory and writes no save format change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Unit tests reject a missing, negative or non-integer index; the dispatch throws a clear error for an out-of-range index; the selftest drives the scroll through Harness.apply and asserts damage, consumption and a turn

[1/3] Add trap discovery state and searchForTraps (3 visible tiles, one turn); [2/3] render revealed traps with a distinct grille, hover card, deck Search button and R hotkey; [3/3] add the harness search action and selftest, inspector proof, docs and ADR-018, then run the UI guard and gates

impact_assessment.why: Traps are concealed until they deal 8-13 damage, so the only counterplay is memorizing the floor or accepting random chip damage; a turn-cost search gives the player agency and makes Deep Fog and Gilded Crypt floors tactical
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can spend a turn to reveal armed traps, route around them, and see what they are on hover; the revealed state survives saves; agents can drive the same search through the harness
impact_assessment.risks: contract: traps gain discovered, the save format gains an additive field, and the action catalog gains search; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: discovered persists, old saves default to false; UI: new deck button and render branch
impact_assessment.mitigation: Harness selftest proves a trap is revealed without triggering and a turn is spent; unit tests cover the search action; save round-trip and inspector checks; UI guard with the full gate set
